Heartily
HAR-ti-lee
adv. (from the soul; with the whole inward man)
Greek ek psuches, literally out of the soul. The Authorized Version's heartily renders a phrase, not a single word, and keeps the Hebraic sense of the inward man as the source of an action rather than merely its accompaniment.

Biblical Definition

And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men. The verse is addressed to servants, and its setting matters: Paul is speaking to men whose labour was owned by somebody else, much of it dull and none of it chosen. To them he says that the quality of the work is to be governed by its true audience. Heartily is out of the soul — the work proceeding from the inward man, not merely passing through the hands. The contrast Paul draws in the parallel passage is exact: not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart. Eyeservice is work calibrated to observation, which slackens the moment the master turns away. Work done as to the Lord cannot slacken, because the Lord never turns away. Two consequences follow, and both cut against instinct. The commonest labour is elevated: whatsoever ye do takes in the field, the kitchen, and the ledger, and Paul immediately adds the reason — for ye serve the Lord Christ. And the Christian's reward is relocated: ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance, from a Master who sees the work no man ever saw. This is the doctrine of vocation in a single adverb.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): from the heart; with all the heart; with sincerity; with zeal; actively; vigorously.

expand to see more

HEARTILY, adv. From the heart; with all the heart; with sincerity; really.

HEARTILY, adv. With zeal; actively; vigorously; earnestly.

HEART, n. The inner part of anything; the seat of the affections and passions; the will; the whole inward man.

EYESERVICE, n. Service performed only under inspection, or the eye of an employer.

MENPLEASER, n. One who is solicitous to please men, rather than to please God.

Key Scripture

Colossians 3:23 — "And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;"

Colossians 3:24 — "Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ."

Ephesians 6:6 — "Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;"

1 Corinthians 10:31 — "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God."

Modern Corruption

The verse is pressed into service for career ambition, as if hearty work meant advancement; and the doctrine of vocation is narrowed until only church work counts as service to Christ.

expand to see more

Colossians 3:23 is a favourite of the success literature, where it becomes a warrant for excellence as a route to promotion. Paul's addressees could not be promoted. They were bondservants, and the reward he names is the inheritance, given by the Lord, not the master. The verse does not promise that hearty work will be noticed or rewarded in this life; it says the audience has changed, and therefore the standard has. Read as a productivity maxim it loses the very thing that made it bearable to the men who first heard it.

The narrowing error runs the other way and is common in the churches: a tacit ranking in which ministry and missions are service to Christ while ordinary labour is merely permitted. The apostle knows nothing of it. Whatsoever ye do takes in every lawful calling, and the reason given — for ye serve the Lord Christ — is said to slaves at their work, not to officers at theirs. The Reformers recovered this against the medieval elevation of the cloister above the household, and the recovery needs making again in every generation, since the instinct to grade callings is perennial.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek psuche (G5590), soul; ergazomai (G2038), to work; ophthalmodouleia (G3787), eyeservice; anthropareskos (G441), menpleaser.

expand to see more

Greek ek psuches (G1537, G5590) — out of the soul; the phrase rendered heartily.

Greek ergazomai (G2038) — to labour, to work at; the verb of ordinary daily toil.

Greek ophthalmodouleia (G3787) — eye-service, work done only while watched.

Greek anthropareskos (G441) — a man-pleaser; one whose audience is human.

Greek kleronomia (G2817) — inheritance; the reward named to men who owned nothing.

Usage

"“do it heartily, as to the Lord” — the audience that fixes the standard."

"“not with eyeservice, as menpleasers” — the contrast, stated plainly."

"“for ye serve the Lord Christ” — said to slaves about their daily work."
